issue_request: FHIR-13029 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification Financial Management issue from DSTU2 asking whether the Claim resource name and Scope and Usage text should clarify how a Claim instance is used as a claim, preauthorization, or predetermination and how a recipient knows which role applies.
initial_application: No current git commit mentioning FHIR-13029 was found. The Claim introduction appears to have been changed in 39b2cdba027 on 2018-02-27 to say that the Claim resource may be interpreted differently depending on intended use and that Claim.use contains the code to indicate that use. Commit c724efa1d90 on 2018-07-10 retained that clarification while refining the role list and adding broader Claim boundaries text.
additional_context: Claim is in current build scope because source/fhir.ini lists claim=Claim under [resources]. Current source/claim/claim-introduction.xml contains the intended-use paragraph, and source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml defines Claim.use with the claim, preauthorization, and predetermination meanings. FHIR-15788 and FHIR-13030 are already represented on the combined branch, and later FHIR-36101 confirms as background that separate preauthorization or predetermination resources are not currently required.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is necessary because the active narrative and conformance source already convey the clarification requested by FHIR-13029.
